intent: Kept unchanged from iteration 10, the best raced geometry (score 146.27): five sensors at x = -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.03 m steps, y = 0.03, 16 mm footprints, wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, body_width 0.12, body_length 0.16, mass 0.75. I am not changing the platform in this final iteration, because the only evidence for any change points away from it. Expected result: the controller's gains will determine the outcome, with progress around the iteration 10 levels and slalom line loss at or below 0.1. Not considered: lower inertia (mass 0.7 or body_length 0.14), which gave slalom line loss of 0.85; and wheel_track 0.10, which lost progress at every gain tried.
learning: Iteration 10 shows that the midpoint inertia (mass 0.75, body_length 0.16) on the 0.12 track improves progress without line loss on slalom, so the inertia lever was used at the right step. Narrow track and low inertia are both ruled out by data. The remaining gains are likely in the controller, since max_error does not move with any geometry tried. The unseen-track result will test whether this platform generalises.
rationale: Iteration 10 raced the midpoint inertia (mass 0.75, body_length 0.16) on the wheel_track 0.12 platform and scored 146.27, the best of the run and 34.5 above iteration 9's reproduced baseline of 111.80. Oval progress rose to 0.597 with 3 of 20 runs finishing. Slalom line loss was 0.0, and s-bend progress was 0.146 with no line loss. The Integrator's stated rule was: if slalom line loss is 0.1 or below, do not go lower on inertia. That condition holds at 0.0, so I am not reducing inertia further. The Integrator's other suggestion, a controller-only change, is theirs to make, and I am not changing the platform again. Iterations 6 to 8 showed that wheel_track 0.10 was worse at every gain, and iteration 4 showed that mass 0.7 with body_length 0.14 drove slalom line loss to 0.85, so both stay excluded. Max_error stayed at 0.061 to 0.066 m across every geometry, which points to the run-ending threshold rather than a geometry lever. This is the final iteration, and the unseen-track race is scored on whatever I deliver. The best-measured geometry is the safest choice, so I am keeping iteration 10 unchanged. I did not take a new geometry risk, since no evidence supports one.
